prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1378; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a low-speed collision in the north parking lot of the insured's retail location. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness the morning after the incident. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Initial contact made by phone; claimant prefers written correspondence going forward.

Entry 2: Recorded statement obtained from claimant. Claimant states the other vehicle backed out of a space without signaling and made contact with the driver's side rear quarter panel. Claimant reports immediate neck discomfort, later described as whiplash-type symptoms with headaches on turning. Claimant has not yet sought medical treatment. Advised claimant to schedule an evaluation with a physician and keep records of all visits and expenses.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles received from claimant and reviewed. Damage consistent with a low-speed rear-quarter impact. Scene diagram requested from insured's facility management. Parking lot surveillance footage requested; facility reports footage is retained for a limited window and copy has been sent for review.

Entry 4: Claimant provided medical intake paperwork indicating a diagnosis of cervical strain consistent with whiplash. Treatment plan includes physical therapy sessions. Claimant asked general questions about the claims process and was informed of the right to seek legal advice at any time. Claimant declined to commit to a settlement discussion until treatment is complete.

Entry 5: Adverse party's insurer contacted and liability acceptance under review based on footage and statements. Repair estimate received and under evaluation. Bodily injury portion remains open pending treatment records and final medical report. Next follow-up set for the coming week to check on claimant's treatment progress and request outstanding documents.
